correctness.rationale: Rooted trees realize every positive contiguous level profile with level zero equal to 1, by assigning all vertices at each level to one parent at the previous level. Adding a common positive baseline to the positive and negative parts of each coefficient therefore realizes the exact polynomial difference, including coefficient gaps. P(1)=0 proves equal component sizes, and two singletons handle P=0. The sign decides which guru prevails when ballots differ; a fair tie yields the average competency. The specified simple internal zeros with positive last interval give exactly m maximizing components. Every fixed finite grid leaves a closed rational subinterval in its complement, on whose interior the second constructed integer polynomial is positive and nowhere else. The six-voter star versus path difference is t(1−t). For at most five voters, two gurus have a fixed weight ordering on (0,1]. Three gurus either retain ordinary majority or a single heavier guru crosses the other two combined weights once; ties average the two rules. With just one delegator and three gurus, the possible tie is only at 1, and all interior voting rules are identical to that at 0. Four gurus with one delegator have a fixed rule on (0,1]: in a 2–2 split the larger guru prevails, and a 3–1 split remains a majority win. One guru or no delegators makes the rule constant. Thus there is no strict interior advantage over both endpoints for any competencies in the smaller forests.
residual_risks: The reported 1,441-forest script run was not independently executed; the finite minimality is decided by the exhaustive rule-level case split. The sharp cutoff concerns only fair-tie voting on acyclic forests and strict superiority over both endpoints.

originality.rationale: Prior viscous-democracy work introduced the accuracy problem, exhibits an interior optimum, recognizes interval-wise behavior, and empirically samples a fixed grid. The supported distinct results are exact two-tree polynomial universality with equal sizes, arbitrarily many optimal components, the uniform worst-case fixed-grid gap, and the sharp six-voter boundary.
residual_risks: A broad multiple-viscosity-optima search was unavailable, not a negative result. Other parameterized Katz-like ranking results or unindexed equivalent constructions could exist.

value.rationale: An exact universality result constrains what structural simplifications are possible in a natural optimization problem. It turns a known example of an interior optimum into unbounded topology of the optimal set and a uniform 1/10 obstruction to graph-independent grid sampling, even with just two ballots. The exact first forest size for a strict interior advantage also distinguishes the phenomenon from arbitrary larger constructions.
residual_risks: The grid obstruction does not apply to adaptive algorithms using the known polynomial or to a priori degree or branching restrictions.
